question: How should a failed-cron dismissal re-arm when the Control UI does not observe the job’s recovery before it fails again?
rationale: Job IDs alone cannot distinguish later incidents, while adding run timestamps would repeatedly resurface persistently failing jobs; the permanent snooze semantics therefore require a product-level incident or expiry rule.

options.title: Add bounded re-arm
options.body: Store dismissal time and expire or re-arm failed-cron snoozes after a defined interval so later incidents eventually surface without nagging on every failed run.

options.title: Use incident generations
options.body: Derive a stable failure-generation identity from an authoritative cron transition field, if the runtime contract can reliably distinguish recovery and recurrence.

options.title: Keep observed-clear semantics
options.body: Accept that recurrence only resurfaces after a tab observes recovery, and narrow the PR’s user-facing claims and tests to that limitation.

recommendation.title: Add bounded re-arm
recommendation.body: Store dismissal time and expire or re-arm failed-cron snoozes after a defined interval so later incidents eventually surface without nagging on every failed run.
